WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that a recorded HOLD is still enforced when the same ledger carries a ruling the planner cannot schedule against. Both cases hold the same two issues and a ledger containing the same slug ruling; the only difference is whether a NUMERIC hold sits beside it. A planner that reads the ledger reports the hold in one and nothing in the other.

WHY IT EXISTS. Every entry was keyed `latest[int(e['issue'])] = e`, so a ruling whose subject is not a number did not merely go unrecorded - int() raised and the whole ledger was rejected, taking every other ruling with it. The wave's own residual rule routes small in-lane findings to a fix rather than a ticket, and that work still reaches a gate, so the better a wave follows its own don't-file-it rule the more of its decisions land in a file one bad line can disable.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH. Nothing about the PRODUCER: no GATE token can emit a slug subject today, because flow-wave-lexicon.sh still refuses a non-numeric subject, and that half is deferred on a lane constraint. The fixtures are hand-written ledgers, which is a genuine input this reader already accepts rather than a stand-in. Nothing about whether the RULING ITSELF is right - only that one unplannable entry no longer silences the rest. Nothing about the reason-harvesting defect (#1189 defect 1), which lives in the lexicon.

THE CASES NAME NO ANSWER: each holds an issues.json and a verdicts.json and nothing else. The runner passes the planner's own exit through.

anchors.why: The planner as it stood before #1189, vendored from 250d56f. MEASURED against both cases: it MISSES the known-bad input, reporting no hold, because it refuses the ledger outright on the slug entry. Note what the runner has to get right for that to be a miss rather than an unavailability: the pre-fix planner exits 2, and exit 2 is two different answers. 'cannot read verdict ledger' on this input is the defect - it read a readable file and threw it away - while any other exit 2 is a gate that could not run. Scoring the first as `unavailable` would record the blind planner as unable to look, when it looked and discarded the record.
